code: # stable version install.packages("gtfsio")  # development version remotes::install_github("r-transit/gtfsio") library(gtfsio) data_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "gtfsio") list.files(data_dir) #> [1] "bad_gtfs.zip"       "blank_lines.zip"    "ggl_gtfs.zip"       #> [4] "locations_feed.zip" "macosx.zip"         "na_strings.zip"     #> [7] "nested_gtfs.zip"    "subdirectories.zip"

title: Introduction to gtfsio
text: read feed use import_gtfs() function. takes either local path URL GTFS .zip file returns GTFS object (, basically, list data frames): function reads, default, .txt files contained .zip file. Alternatively, can specify files read files argument (note: without .txt extension): Similarly, can use fields argument read selective fields file. arguments can combined, offering great deal flexibility can translate fast reading times. fields parsed according standards reading writing GTFS feeds R. Undocumented files fields (.e. specified GTFS reference) read character, default. can overrule default extra_spec (note undocumented fields specified argument). ggl_gtfs.zip contains undocumented field levels.txt file, named elevation. Let’s check effect extra_spec:
code: gtfs_path <- file.path(data_dir, "ggl_gtfs.zip") gtfs_url  <- "https://github.com/r-transit/gtfsio/raw/master/inst/extdata/ggl_gtfs.zip"  gtfs_from_path <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path) names(gtfs_from_path) #>  [1] "calendar_dates"  "fare_attributes" "fare_rules"      "feed_info"       #>  [5] "frequencies"     "levels"          "pathways"        "routes"          #>  [9] "shapes"          "stop_times"      "stops"           "transfers"       #> [13] "translations"    "trips"           "agency"          "attributions"    #> [17] "calendar"  gtfs_from_url <- import_gtfs(gtfs_url) names(gtfs_from_url) #>  [1] "calendar_dates"  "fare_attributes" "fare_rules"      "feed_info"       #>  [5] "frequencies"     "levels"          "pathways"        "routes"          #>  [9] "shapes"          "stop_times"      "stops"           "transfers"       #> [13] "translations"    "trips"           "agency"          "attributions"    #> [17] "calendar" gtfs <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path, files = c("shapes", "trips"))  gtfs #> $shapes #>    shape_id shape_pt_lat shape_pt_lon shape_pt_sequence shape_dist_traveled #>      <char>        <num>        <num>             <int>               <num> #> 1:    A_shp     37.61956    -122.4816                 1              0.0000 #> 2:    A_shp     37.64430    -122.4107                 2              6.8310 #> 3:    A_shp     37.65863    -122.3084 Downtown        1 #> 2:        A         WE    AWE2      Downtown        2 gtfs <- import_gtfs(   gtfs_path,   files = c("shapes", "trips"),   fields = list(trips = c("trip_id", "route_id")) )  gtfs #> $shapes #>    shape_id shape_pt_lat shape_pt_lon shape_pt_sequence shape_dist_traveled #>      <char>        <num>        <num>             <int>               <num> #> 1:    A_shp     37.61956    -122.4816                 1              0.0000 #> 2:    A_shp     37.64430    -122.4107                 2              6.8310 #> 3:    A_shp     37.65863    -122.3084                 3             15.8765 #>  #> $trips #>    trip_id route_id #>     <char>   <char> #> 1:    AWE1        A #> 2:    AWE2        A gtfs <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path, files = "levels")  gtfs$levels #>    level_id level_index level_name elevation #>      <char>       <num>     <char>    <char> #> 1:       L0           0     Street         0 #> 2:       L1          -1  Mezzanine        -6 #> 3:       L2          -2 Southbound       -18 #> 4:       L3          -3 Northbound       -24  class(gtfs$levels$elevation) #> [1] "character"  gtfs <- import_gtfs(   gtfs_path,    files = "levels",    extra_spec = list(levels = c(elevation = "integer")) )  gtfs$levels #>    level_id level_index level_name elevation #>      <char>       <num>     <char>     <int> #> 1:       L0           0     Street         0 #> 2:       L1          -1  Mezzanine        -6 #> 3:       L2          -2 Southbound       -18 #> 4:       L3          -3 Northbound       -24  class(gtfs$levels$elevation) #> [1] "integer"

title: Introduction to gtfsio
text: Use export_gtfs() write GTFS object disk. Please note function assumes object formatted according standards reading writing GTFS feeds R - .e. ’s , conversions done using export_gtfs(). Objects written .zip feeds default, can also write directories using as_dir argument: function defaults writing every element inside GTFS object .txt file. import_gtfs(), use files argument overrule behaviour: can also use standard_only argument export files fields specified GTFS reference (.e. leave undocumented files/fields). example , extra_gtfs contains undocumented file (extra_file) undocumented field regular file (levels$elevation) written disk using export_gtfs():
code: gtfs <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path) tmpf <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip") tmpd <- tempfile()  export_gtfs(gtfs, tmpf) zip::zip_list(tmpf)$filename #>  [1] "calendar_dates.txt"  "fare_attributes.txt" "fare_rules.txt"      #>  [4] "feed_info.txt"       "frequencies.txt"     "levels.txt"          #>  [7] "pathways.txt"        "routes.txt"          "shapes.txt"          #> [10] "stop_times.txt"      "stops.txt"           "transfers.txt"       #> [13] "translations.txt"    "trips.txt"           "agency.txt"          #> [16] "attributions.txt"    "calendar.txt"  export_gtfs(gtfs, tmpd, as_dir = TRUE) list.files(tmpd) #>  [1] "agency.txt"          "attributions.txt"    "calendar_dates.txt"  #>  [4] "calendar.txt"        "fare_attributes.txt" "fare_rules.txt"      #>  [7] "feed_info.txt"       "frequencies.txt"     "levels.txt"          #> [10] "pathways.txt"        "routes.txt"          "shapes.txt"          #> [13] "stop_times.txt"      "stops.txt"           "transfers.txt"       #> [16] "translations.txt"    "trips.txt" export_gtfs(gtfs, tmpf, files = c("shapes", "trips")) zip::zip_list(tmpf)$filename #> [1] "shapes.txt" "trips.txt" extra_gtfs <- gtfs extra_gtfs$extra_file <- data.frame(column = "value")  export_gtfs(extra_gtfs, tmpd, as_dir = TRUE, standard_only = TRUE)  "extra_file" %in% sub(".txt", "", list.files(tmpd)) #> [1] FALSE  levels_fields <- readLines(file.path(tmpd, "levels.txt"), n = 1L) grepl("elevation", levels_fields) #> [1] FALSE

title: Introduction to gtfsio
text: gtfsio also includes functions check structure GTFS objects. check_file_exists() checks existence elements representing specific text files inside object. returns TRUE check successful, FALSE otherwise. assert_file_exists() invisibly returns object successful, throws error otherwise: check_field_exists() checks existence fields, represented columns, inside GTFS objects. returns TRUE check successful, FALSE otherwise. assert_field_exists() invisibly returns object successful, throws error otherwise: check_field_class() checks classes fields inside GTFS objects. returns TRUE check successful, FALSE otherwise. assert_field_class() invisibly returns object successful, throws error otherwise: Please notes “lower-level” checks conducted inside function - e.g. checking type field, first existence field checked: functions great package interoperability. two distinct packages represent GTFS text files using data structure (gtfstools gtfsrouter use data.tables, example), just need add basic checks proceeding operations objects created package. , gtfsrouter requires transfers element perform operations, might well perform object created gtfstools, long contains transfers element. Thus, greatly benefit assert_*/check_* calls proceeding operations.
code: gtfs <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path, files = c("shapes", "trips"))  check_file_exists(gtfs, "shapes") #> [1] TRUE check_file_exists(gtfs, "stop_times") #> [1] FALSE  assert_file_exists(gtfs, "shapes") assert_file_exists(gtfs, "stop_times") #> Error: #> ! The GTFS object is missing the following required element(s): 'stop_times' gtfs <- import_gtfs(   gtfs_path,   files = "trips",   fields = list(trips = "trip_id") )  check_field_exists(gtfs, "trips", fields = "trip_id") #> [1] TRUE check_field_exists(gtfs, "trips", fields = "shape_id") #> [1] FALSE  assert_field_exists(gtfs, "trips", fields = "trip_id") assert_field_exists(gtfs, "trips", fields = "shape_id") #> Error: #> ! The GTFS object 'trips' element is missing the following required column(s): 'shape_id' gtfs <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path, files = "levels")  check_field_class(gtfs, "levels", fields = "elevation", classes = "character") #> [1] TRUE check_field_class(gtfs, "levels", fields = "elevation", classes = "integer") #> [1] FALSE  assert_field_class(gtfs, "levels", fields = "elevation", classes = "character") assert_field_class(gtfs, "levels", fields = "elevation", classes = "integer") #> Error: #> ! The following columns in the GTFS object 'levels' element do not inherit from the required classes: #>   - 'elevation': requires integer, but inherits from character gtfs <- import_gtfs(gtfs_path, files = "shapes")  check_field_class(gtfs, "stop_times", fields = "stop_id", classes = "character") #> [1] FALSE  assert_field_class(gtfs, "stop_times", fields = "stop_id", classes = "character") #> Error: #> ! The GTFS object is missing the following required element(s): 'stop_times'
